newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Washington Post page one - April 3.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Washington Post page one - April 3.

text.p: The Washington Post carries the following stories on its front page April 3:

WASHINGTON - Simple blood test can help identify healthy people most likely to have a heart attack or stroke years before classic warning signs appear, new research suggests, lending support to radical new theory about underlying causes of these leading killers.

BALTIMORE - Cal Ripken of the Baltimore Orioles, perhaps the most beloved figure in U.S. baseball, signed a two-year contract extension that virtually guarantees he'll finish his career playing for the team he started with, a rarity.
WASHINGTON - Breakdown of Middle East peace negotiations is forcing Clinton administration to confront thorny issues of Jewish settlements in occupied territories and status of Jerusalem.
NEW YORK - Pragmatic Republican mayors of New York and Los Angeles opened doors to change, not conservative rebellion.
WASHINGTON - First Union Corp. banks are requiring thumb prints to cash checks at local branches.
WASHINGTON - Many black professionals says they must hide their heritage to fit in, get ahead in corporate culture shaped by whites.
PARIS - France's protective labor laws hamper economic downsizing.
